subject: Performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification — hosted vs current provider (post-demo recap)
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification — hosted vs current provider (post-demo recap)

Hi Samir — thanks again for the demo call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a side-by-side performance qualification running: 

Summary of what we heard from your side:
- Primary goal: user-facing chat where end-to-end (client -> model -> client) latency meets strict SLOs for interactive UX.
- Target SLOs you asked us to validate: p95 < 200ms end-to-end, p99 < 500ms for typical user flows (avg request ~512 tokens generated, streaming enabled).
- Throughput/traffic: sustained 50–75 req/s during business hours, with bursts up to ~300 req/s; concurrent streaming connections expected ~200–300.
- Current provider observed behavior: p95 ~450ms, p99 ~1.2s (under burst/concurrency), and noticeable tail regressions under load.

What Redwood proposes for the qualification:
1) Side-by-side perf run (48–72 hours): we run the Redwood hosted stack against a representative prompt set and your sample traffic to measure real p95/p99 E2E latency with streaming.
2) Test artifacts: you share a small sample of tokenized prompts + traffic CSV and we provide our perf harness config (attached: perf-tests-summary.pdf + redwood-perf-harness-config.yaml).
3) Measurement points: end-to-end wall clock (client request -> first token out / final token out), first-byte streaming latency, per-token throughput, p95/p99 for both first-byte and completion, and concurrency/CPU/GPU utilization.
4) Optional: dedicated capacity quote if you want a guaranteed baseline for the trial window to remove noisy multi-tenant effects.

Open questions for you: 
- Can you share the traffic sample and a representative prompt set (e.g., 200–500 sample prompts) so we can re-run exactly what you saw?
- Do you require the test to run through your VPC / private networking (we can accommodate via Private deployment or a peering arrangement)?

Next steps suggested: Samir to share the sample traffic + any special networking/legal constraints; Redwood (Dev/Aditya) to respond with a proposed test config and expected baseline numbers; schedule test window (target week of Dec 1)

Attaching a short summary of the perf approach and preliminary numbers we typically see for similar workloads (perf-tests-summary.pdf).

Thanks — I’ll loop in Marissa and Aditya for commercial/ops context.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: perf-tests-summary.pdf (PDF, 230KB)

From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@finlytics.com>

Cc: FinLytics Eng <eng@finlytics.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification — hosted vs current provider (post-demo recap)

Thanks Laura — quick clarifications from our side. Appreciate the clear plan. 

1) Streaming: our UX depends heavily on low first-byte latency for perceived responsiveness. For the 512-token flows we saw first-byte times of ~120–180ms on the current provider, which led to a choppy experience. We’re aiming for first-byte <= 50ms ideally, and p95/p99 for full completion as you listed.
2) Traffic sample: attaching a redacted sample of our traffic profile (finlytics-traffic-sample.csv). The CSV includes timestamps, payload sizes, and concurrency traces.
3) Networking: initially we can run the perf tests over public endpoints (TLS). If numbers look good, we’ll plan a VPC test — our security team will need a brief network diagram and cert/KMS notes.

One ask: can you call out the delta we should expect between Redwood hosted and what we observed on our current provider? That will help us set internal expectations before doing a full run.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Khan
Head of Platform
FinLytics

--
Attachment: finlytics-traffic-sample.csv (CSV, 18KB)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@finlytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification — hosted vs current provider (post-demo recap)

Hi Samir — quick technical note on expected baselines and the recommended test configuration. We’ll provide the perf harness and exact config but here are realistic numbers you can expect on Redwood hosted for a 512-token generation workload (streaming enabled) using our rw-optimized models and typical production serving stack: 

Typical Redwood hosted baselines (observed across multiple customers on similar workloads):
- End-to-end p95 (completion): ~110–140ms
- End-to-end p99 (completion): ~240–300ms
- First-byte (streaming start) median: ~28–45ms; p95 ~60–80ms
- Sustained throughput per instance (single pod): ~70–90 req/s for 512-token workloads (batching + kv-cache engaged)
- Concurrency per node: comfortably supports ~150–250 concurrent streaming connections with autoscaling to cover bursts.
- Cache impact: KV/prefix cache reduces cost and tail for repeated prompts — expect ~40–60% improvement on repeated prefixes depending on your prompt reuse.

Compared to the numbers you reported from your current provider (p95 ~450ms, p99 ~1.2s), the Redwood hosted stack typically shows a ~2–4x improvement on p95 and similar on p99 in many screened workloads — main drivers are optimized kernels, per-request fast-paths, and prefix caching. 

Important test config notes:
- We measure true E2E from the client side (TLS handshake excluded) with an agent that matches your client batching/keepalive behavior.
- Streaming test includes sending the prompt and measuring first-byte TO first token and final completion.
- For fairness, we’ll reproduce your concurrency pattern from finlytics-traffic-sample.csv and run three load phases: baseline (sustained), burst, and recovery.

I’ve attached the perf harness config we’ll run (redwood-perf-harness-config.yaml). If you’re happy, propose a 48–72 hour window starting Dec 1 — we’ll spin up a dedicated test pool for the window to ensure clean comparatives. After the run we’ll provide per-test p50/p95/p99, token-level traces, and utilization dashboards.

Let me know if you need TLS mutual auth for the VPC stage or any special headers we should mirror.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior SRE, Performance
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: redwood-perf-harness-config.yaml (YAML, 4KB)
